title: Signal Health Orchestrator for Embedding Accuracy and Drift Detection
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build an orchestration layer and job set that continuously evaluates embedding quality and reranker stability across production traffic slices. This ticket implements the Signal Health Orchestrator: a configurable pipeline that (1) manages curated seed golden sets and sample pools, (2) runs deterministic offline metrics and stochastic perturbation probes, (3) surfaces drift signals with context (latency, model variant, region, request shape) and (4) triggers automated alerts and canary gating for reranker rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can run nightly jobs over production-sampled corpora and seeded golden sets without manual intervention
Produce and store a daily embedding-quality report (Spearman, Kendall, Recall@k, MRR) broken down by region/model/route
Detect introduced regressions with >80% precision on synthetic perturbation tests and generate an alert to #ml-ops when thresholds are crossed
Integrate a canary gate: if embedding stability (top-K overlap) drops below threshold for 3 consecutive runs, block automatic reranker rollout and create ENG ticket
Dashboards show time series and highlight correlates: median latency, batch size, token length, and model variant
Evidence of end-to-end pipeline in CI: scheduled job, artifact retention, and a smoke PR that validates outputs against golden checksums
technical_plan: Design data selection strategy: combine reservoir sampling of recent production requests, stratified sampling by route/tenant, and a stewarded seed golden set
Implement a job graph in existing batch runner that runs: embedding extract -> normalization checks -> pairwise similarity metrics -> reranker scoring comparison
Add synthetic perturbation module: token swaps, punctuation noise, paraphrase injection to estimate robustness and calibration drift
Map telemetry dimensions to signals: include latency, batch size, kernel selection, GPU type, and model quantization variant
Persist all outputs to S3 with standardized schema and save derived aggregates to metrics DB for dashboarding
Add an evaluation runner that computes ranking metrics (MRR, MAP, Recall@k), correlation with human labels (Spearman), and stability measures (top-K Jaccard/overlap)
metrics: Spearman correlation with annotated pairs (daily): target >= 0.78, alert if < 0.72
Recall@10 on golden set: target >= 0.85, alert if delta vs baseline > 0.05
Median top-1 cosine similarity on anchor corpus: track drift percentage over 7/30/90d windows
Top-K stability (K=50) Jaccard between consecutive runs: alert if drop > 0.12
False-positive rate for synthetic perturbation detector: target < 0.20
End-to-end job latency: nightly run should finish within 2 hours for 10M-sample corpus; scale targets defined for larger corpora
milestones: M1 (2025-02-21): schema and sample selection spec approved; stewarded golden set format defined
M2 (2025-02-28): core offline runner implemented and computes baseline metrics on historical snapshot
M3 (2025-03-07): synthetic perturbation module integrated; initial alerting rules created
M4 (2025-03-14): dashboard panels and canary gating wired; smoke end-to-end CI job added
M5 (2025-03-15): handoff and runbook drafted; operational on-call notified
risks: Golden-set bias: seed goldens might not represent long-tail user queries, causing missed drift — mitigate by steward rotation and periodic sampling refresh
Cost and scale: running large nightly jobs could spike infra cost — mitigate with sampled nightly + full weekly runs
Metric sensitivity: some metrics (e.g., Spearman) are sensitive to label noise — maintain human-annotated validation slices and bootstrap confidence intervals
False alarms: perturbation probes may trigger noisy alerts for non-impactful changes — tune thresholds and require 3-run confirmation
Privacy/GDPR: retention of sampled queries may include PII — ensure redaction pipeline and TTL for raw captures
